Everyone keeps warning that junior developers are about to disappear while seniors pull further ahead, and there is real pressure at the entry level. Looking closely at how people actually learn with these tools, though, the picture is less one-sided than it looks.

Experienced engineers definitely have a head start right now. When you have been through a few production projects, you learn the hard way about DNS records, DMARC and DKIM, free-tier hosting or database traps that sting you later, setting up a VPS with key-only SSH, locking out brute force attacks, tuning Nginx, dealing with vulnerabilities that could expose client data, or adjusting database memory limits. Starting from that base of experience, and knowing how to communicate a problem clearly, lets a senior turn AI into massive leverage.

Where juniors benefit is in how fast they can close that gap. Less experienced builders usually run into trouble not because they lack ambition, but because they do not yet know what long-term implications to think ahead about. Now an AI assistant can point those second-order risks out in real time, and the next time that person builds something, they remember. Even people who struggle to articulate their ideas early on get nudged by the machine to consider more options and reason through problems more clearly. In the same way older developers learned through slow trial and error, newer ones can pick up those lessons much faster, and research backs this up: the MIT and Stanford study of over 5,000 workers by Brynjolfsson, Li, and Raymond found that less experienced workers gained the most from generative AI (up to 34% faster resolution), absorbing patterns from top performers and moving up the learning curve quicker.

Hiring is already starting to reflect that shift. Anthropic are no longer doing coding interviews systematically for every engineer, because ideas and judgment are what they are looking for while the code itself is handled and checked elsewhere. Experienced developers may well become 30x or 50x more productive, while juniors get a faster leg up into operating at a 10x level and following in the path of seniors, just along a very different path than the one seniors had to trailblaze on their own.
